svg.aria-label: Finalize cutover changes a status, discards all replicated data and terminates the replication infrastructure, so reverting afterwards restores the label but not the ability to go back
svg.title: In AWS Transform MGN the rollback plan depends on the source server still replicating. Finalizing a cutover does three things in one sentence: it changes the migration lifecycle status to Cutover complete, stops data replication and causes all replicated data to be discarded, and terminates all AWS resources used for data replication. Reverting a finalized cutover returns the lifecycle status to Ready for cutover, but the replicated data is gone and the infrastructure holding it was terminated, so revert restores the label rather than the capability. The freeze window therefore ends when you finalise, not when the instances start serving traffic.

g.text: One sentence, three actions, and only one of them is bookkeeping
Finalize cutover
1. Status → Cutover complete
bookkeeping, harmless
2. Replicated data discarded
the copy you would return to
3. Replication resources terminated
nothing left to resume from
What you think revert does
Undo the cutover. Put the rollback
plan back the way it was.
Fail back to the source server,
which is still replicating.
What revert does
Sets the lifecycle status back to
Ready for cutover. That is all.
The data was discarded and the
infrastructure terminated.
So the freeze window is not the cutover window
It lasts as long as the source is somewhere you could return to, and that ends when you finalise.
Size it by the slowest business cycle that could still reject the migration — month end, the weekly job.
